title: igr run configuration (schema 1)
description: Generated from igr_cli/registry.py by `igr describe --schema`. Do not edit by hand.

seed.description: Random seed, recorded in the run directory. No model in this package draws random numbers from it: trajectory and projection are deterministic and the experiment scripts use their own fixed seeds. Always set it anyway, so runs stay reproducible if a stochastic model is added.

sweep.description: Optional, used only by `sweep`: {dotted.parameter: [values, ...]}; the cartesian product is run, one run directory per point.

kind.description: Which fitness function f(x) to use. Its parameters go in the block fitness.<kind> (only that block is allowed). Kinds: quadratic: f(x) = 0.30 x - 0.20 x^2; perturbed_quadratic: f(x) = a x - b x^2 + eps sin(k x); polynomial: f(x) = sum_i coefficients[i] x^i; sinusoid: f(x) = eps sin(k x); multimodal: f(x) = sum_c exp(-(x - c)^2 / (2 width^2)); stalling: f(x) = -(x^2 - a^2)^2; rational_conjugate: f(x) = (alpha z + beta z^2)/(nu + z^2) + gamma, z = (x - mu)/sigma; quadratic_rational_homotopy: f_s(x) = (1 - s) x^2 + s x^2/(nu + x^2).

a.description: [perturbed_quadratic: f(x) = a x - b x^2 + eps sin(k x)] Linear coefficient. Moves the mean.

b.description: [perturbed_quadratic: f(x) = a x - b x^2 + eps sin(k x)] Quadratic coefficient (f contains -b x^2). b > 0 is concave; b < 0 is convex and, with eps = 0, the Gaussian variance blows up at t* = 1/(2|b| var0) (Eq. 50).

eps.description: [perturbed_quadratic: f(x) = a x - b x^2 + eps sin(k x)] Perturbation amplitude. eps = 0 is exactly Gaussian-invariant; the defect grows with |eps| (Fig S3b). Experiments use 0 to 0.8.

k.description: [perturbed_quadratic: f(x) = a x - b x^2 + eps sin(k x)] Perturbation wavenumber.

coefficients.description: [polynomial: f(x) = sum_i coefficients[i] x^i] Polynomial coefficients c0, c1, c2, ... (increasing degree). At least one entry.

width.description: [multimodal: f(x) = sum_c exp(-(x - c)^2 / (2 width^2))] Bump width (standard deviation of each bump). Experiments use 0.6.

centers.description: [multimodal: f(x) = sum_c exp(-(x - c)^2 / (2 width^2))] Bump centers in trait units. Unit: trait units (x).

a.description: [stalling: f(x) = -(x^2 - a^2)^2] Well location +/- a. The Gaussian surrogate stalls at N(0, a^2/3) (set state.var or initial.var yourself).

alpha.description: [rational_conjugate: f(x) = (alpha z + beta z^2)/(nu + z^2) + gamma, z = (x - mu)/sigma] Coefficient of z.

beta.description: [rational_conjugate: f(x) = (alpha z + beta z^2)/(nu + z^2) + gamma, z = (x - mu)/sigma] Coefficient of z^2.

gamma.description: [rational_conjugate: f(x) = (alpha z + beta z^2)/(nu + z^2) + gamma, z = (x - mu)/sigma] Additive constant (does not change any defect or trajectory).

mu.description: [rational_conjugate: f(x) = (alpha z + beta z^2)/(nu + z^2) + gamma, z = (x - mu)/sigma] Center of z, trait units. Unit: trait units (x).

sigma.description: [rational_conjugate: f(x) = (alpha z + beta z^2)/(nu + z^2) + gamma, z = (x - mu)/sigma] Scale of z, trait units. Unit: trait units (x).

nu.description: [rational_conjugate: f(x) = (alpha z + beta z^2)/(nu + z^2) + gamma, z = (x - mu)/sigma] Degrees of freedom of the conjugate Student-t family.

s.description: [quadratic_rational_homotopy: f_s(x) = (1 - s) x^2 + s x^2/(nu + x^2)] Homotopy parameter, quadratic (0) to rational (1).

nu.description: [quadratic_rational_homotopy: f_s(x) = (1 - s) x^2 + s x^2/(nu + x^2)] nu of the rational endpoint.

a.description: Left end of the uniform quadrature grid. All densities live on [a, b]; mass outside is truncated. Unit: trait units (x).

b.description: Right end of the quadrature grid. Unit: trait units (x).

n.description: Number of grid points (trapezoidal quadrature). Cost scales linearly with n. Experiments use 2401 to 60001.

mu.description: Mean of the initial Gaussian density rho0 = N(mu0, var0). Unit: trait units (x).

var.description: Variance of the initial Gaussian density. Unit: trait units squared.

t_end.description: Final replicator time. The exact tilt is evaluated and the surrogate ODEs integrated on [0, t_end]. Unit: replicator time (1/fitness units; t multiplies f in rho0*exp(t f)).

n_points.description: Number of equally spaced output times in [0, t_end], including both ends.

surrogates.description: Gaussian surrogates to integrate and compare with the exact tilt. 'param' = Fisher moment flow (Eq. S1); 'proj' = L2(dx) density-velocity projection (comparison only).

rtol.description: Relative tolerance of scipy solve_ivp for the surrogate ODEs.

family.description: Search family of the current state rho_theta and of the base score dictionary.

mu.description: Location of the state density. Unit: trait units (x).

var.description: Variance of the Gaussian state N(mu, var). Experiments use 1.0 and 2.5^2 = 6.25 (broad baseline of S4/S7). Unit: trait units squared.

sigma.description: Scale of the Student-t state. Unit: trait units (x).

nu.description: Degrees of freedom of the Student-t state.

tau.description: Elite fraction (top tau of the quantile range). Larger tau selects more of the population.
Elite fraction (top tau of the quantile range). Larger tau selects more of the population.

h.description: Logistic bandwidth of the smooth elite (README: h = 0.05 is a representative choice).

targets.description: Target signals to project. Shaped targets use the fitness quantile q under the state density (Section 5.1); 'raw' is the unshaped centered fitness.

K.description: Number of rank features (Legendre degree 1..K, or K bins).
Number of rank features (Legendre degree 1..K, or K bins).

centers.description: RBF centers (S7 uses linspace(-4, 4, 9) and linspace(-5, 5, 17)).

h.description: RBF bandwidth (S7 uses 0.8 x center spacing).

dictionaries.description: Score dictionaries. Each is the family's own scores plus an optional augmentation; R^2 rises with richer dictionaries.

ridge.description: Tikhonov ridge added as ridge*mean(diag F)*I to the Gram matrix before the pseudoinverse. Unit: dimensionless.

id.description: Which supplementary experiment group to run (same ids as run_all.py).

nsamples.description: Independent samples per (dictionary, N, lambda) setting in S11. The paper used 150; run_all --quick uses 20. Replaces the IGR_NSAMPLES environment variable.

nmc.description: Monte Carlo sample size for Table S8 (id S18). run_all --quick uses 15000. Replaces the IGR_NMC environment variable.
